# multiCollglm

Collinearity diagnostics for generalized linear models (GLMs), on `glm`
objects or on regularized models fitted with `glmnet` / `cv.glmnet`.

[`condition_number()`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/condition_number.md),
[`bkw_diagnostics()`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/bkw_diagnostics.md)
and
[`rvif_diagnostics()`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/rvif_diagnostics.md)
generalize the classical linear-regression collinearity diagnostics to
any family and link function. By default (`method = "WS"`, Weissfeld and
Sereika, 1991) they are computed on the design matrix weighted by the
IRLS weights at convergence and scaled to unit length by column, without
centering, so the intercept takes part in the diagnosis. The `method`
argument also gives the definition of MacKinnon and Puterman (`"MP"`),
the one of the original design matrix \\X'X\\, unweighted (`"X"`), and
the raw information matrix \\X'WX\\ (`"RAW"`).
[`ml_collinearity()`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/ml_collinearity.md)
adds a fourth, complementary diagnostic, comparing the condition number
of the *original* design matrix against that of the IRLS-weighted
information matrix (Lesaffre and Marx, 1993) to tell apart ordinary
collinearity among the explanatory variables from *ML-collinearity*.

## Installation

``` r

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("cbgarciaugr/multiCollglm")
# or, from a local copy of the package folder:
# remotes::install_local("path/to/multiCollglm_0.4.0")
```

## Quick example

``` r

library(multiCollglm)

mod <- glm(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4, family = Gamma(link = "inverse"), data = data)

condition_number(mod)                  # Weissfeld and Sereika (default)
condition_number(mod, method = "MP")   # MacKinnon and Puterman
condition_number(mod, method = "X")    # original design matrix X'X (unit length)
condition_number(mod, method = "RAW")  # X'WX, no transformation
bkw_diagnostics(mod)
rvif_diagnostics(mod)
ml_collinearity(mod)
```

## Learn more

[`vignette("multiCollglm")`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/articles/multiCollglm.md)
is the package’s complete guide: every function, the four
condition-number definitions available via `method`, the
`glmnet`/`cv.glmnet` interface, and the full ML-collinearity rationale.

The [package website](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/) also
has the [full function
reference](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/index.html)
an article [comparing the package with
VisCollin](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/articles/comparison-viscollin.html)
and a series of [reproduction
articles](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/articles/index.html):
real published cases reproduced with `multiCollglm`, using four example
datasets bundled with the package (`LeeCancer`, `Nitrogen`, `Mine`,
`Plastic`) and a fifth (`Bodyfat`, from the `TH.data` package).

# Package index

## Diagnostics

The three main functions. By default (`method = "WS"`) they use the
design matrix weighted by IRLS at convergence and scaled to unit length
by column, without centering; `method` also gives the definitions of
MacKinnon and Puterman (`"MP"`), of the original design matrix (`"X"`)
and of the raw information matrix (`"RAW"`).

- [`condition_number()`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/condition_number.md)
  : Condition number of a model (collinearity diagnostic)
- [`bkw_diagnostics()`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/bkw_diagnostics.md)
  : Full Belsley-Kuh-Welsch collinearity diagnostics
- [`rvif_diagnostics()`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/rvif_diagnostics.md)
  : Redefined Variance Inflation Factor (RVIF) diagnostics

## ML-collinearity

Compares the condition number of the original design matrix against that
of the IRLS-weighted information matrix, following Lesaffre and Marx
(1993), to tell apart ordinary collinearity among the explanatory
variables from ML-collinearity.

- [`ml_collinearity()`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/ml_collinearity.md)
  : ML-collinearity diagnostic (Lesaffre and Marx, 1993)

## Example datasets

Real data used in the examples (see the Examples menu).

- [`Nitrogen`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/Nitrogen.md)
  : Nitrogen dioxide air-pollution data (Chatterjee and Hadi 1988)
- [`Mine`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/Mine.md)
  : Coal mine roof-fracture data
- [`LeeCancer`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/LeeCancer.md)
  : Lee (1974) cancer remission data
- [`Plastic`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/Plastic.md)
  : Plastic plywood manufacturing process data

## Package

- [`multiCollglm`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/multiCollglm-package.md)
  [`multiCollglm-package`](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/reference/multiCollglm-package.md)
  : multiCollglm: collinearity diagnostics for GLMs and glmnet

# Articles

### Get started

- [Introduction to
  multiCollglm](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/articles/multiCollglm.md):

### Examples

Real-data applications. Start with the overview, which links to each
example and summarizes the four condition-number definitions on all the
data sets.

- [Examples: real-data
  applications](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/articles/examples.md):

  Index of the worked examples of multiCollglm: five reproductions of
  published collinearity diagnostics on real data, and a comparison with
  the VisCollin package, with a summary of the four condition-number
  definitions on every data set.

- [Reproduction: cancer remission data (Lee
  1974)](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/articles/reproduction-lee-cancer.md):

  Reproduces the three logistic-model variants fitted to Lee’s (1974)
  cancer remission dataset – Lesaffre and Marx (1993), Ozkale and Arican
  (2016)/Ozkale (2021), and Huang, Jou and Cho (2015) – and contrasts
  them against multiCollglm’s four methods (WS, MP, X, RAW).

- [Reproduction: Chatterjee and Hadi (1988) -- Nitrogen
  data](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/articles/reproduction-nitrogen.md):

  Reproduces the collinearity diagnostic of the Nitrogen dataset (Gamma,
  inverse link), contrasts it against nine published
  reproductions/variants, and shows how multiCollglm’s four
  condition-number methods (WS, MP, X, RAW) behave, and why centering
  the weighted matrix is not possible for this model.

- [Reproduction: coal mine roof-fracture data
  (Mine)](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/articles/reproduction-mines.md):

  Reproduces the collinearity diagnostic of the coal mine roof-fracture
  dataset, used by five works fitting different count-data GLMs, and
  shows that the “RAW” (untransformed) method exactly reproduces the
  most-cited value in the literature.

- [Reproduction: Bodyfat data
  (TH.data)](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/articles/reproduction-bodyfat.md):

  Reproduces the collinearity diagnostic of the bodyfat dataset (Gamma,
  log link) used by five works, and documents a structural fact about
  the log link for the Gamma family that explains why three of the
  package’s methods coincide exactly in this case.

- [Reproduction: plastic plywood manufacturing data
  (Plastic)](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/articles/reproduction-plastic.md):

  Reproduces the collinearity diagnostic of the plastic plywood
  manufacturing dataset, used by six works fitting different count-data
  GLMs, and documents a citation error (CN = 8634.73) that propagates
  unverified across at least three publications.

### Comparison with other software

How multiCollglm relates to the VisCollin package, on the same data.

- [Comparison with
  VisCollin](https://cbgarciaugr.github.io/multiCollglm/articles/comparison-viscollin.md):

  Compares multiCollglm with the VisCollin package (Friendly), on the
  real datasets of the package: what VisCollin::colldiag() computes when
  it is given a GLM, when it coincides exactly with multiCollglm (method
  = “X”), and where the two diverge (IRLS weights, factors, weights and
  offsets, visualization).
